title: Ug 1.0 on the glazing unit passport: why the whole window of a heritage building may fail the requirement
description: Calculating Uw with frame and glazing edge: instead of Ug 1.0 we get 1.45. How to check the selected heritage window unit and not lose the effect of historic glazing bars.
seo_title: Ug and Uw of a heritage window: glazing unit, frame and edge thermal bridge
seo_description: Calculating Uw with frame and glazing edge: instead of Ug 1.0 we get 1.45. How to check the selected heritage window unit and not lose the effect of historic glazing bars.
seo_keywords: Ug Uw difference, heat transfer of heritage window, glazing unit frame linear bridge, Uw calculation of window unit
content:
The client is offered a window for a historic building with the words "heat transfer 1.0". The confirming document indeed shows 1.0, but next to it is the designation Ug: this is a glazing characteristic. The design constraint applies to the whole window unit, Uw. Substituting the glazing unit value without frame and edge into it is not allowed: in the case considered the result is 1.45, and the requirement of 1.2 is not met.

What the short line of a commercial offer hides

A window specification contains several thermal characteristics. Ug refers to the glazing, Uf to the frame, Uw to the window as a whole. All three coefficients may have the same units W/(m²·K), so the error is not detected by a simple dimensional check. It is important to keep the object to which the number belongs.

In a conditional adaptation project for a cultural heritage site, a requirement is set for a specific window unit: Uw no more than 1.2 W/(m²·K). The applicability of the chosen calculation method and comparability of source characteristics are confirmed. This is a project condition of the example, not a declared universal norm for any monument.

The glazing area Ag is 1.5 m², its Ug is 1.0. The frame area Af is 0.5 m², Uf is 2.0. The total relevant glazing edge length lg is 5 m, the linear coefficient of this node ψg is 0.08 W/(m·K). These dimensions, profile and spacer frame are established. Values from a similar advertising sample are not transferred here.

Calculation in which the edge is not lost

For the adopted model, the unit coefficient is defined by the expression Uw = (Ag × Ug + Af × Uf + lg × ψg) / (Ag + Af). The area part describes the glass and the frame, and the linear term accounts for the additional transfer at the glazing edge. The principle and composition of the calculation are given in the Passive House Institute explanation.

ContributionCalculationResult, W/K
Glazing1.5 × 1.01.5
Frame0.5 × 2.01.0
Glazing edge5 × 0.080.4
Total1.5 + 1.0 + 0.42.9

The total area of the unit is 2 m². Therefore Uw = 2.9 / 2 = 1.45 W/(m²·K). Even if the glass with the frame is taken into account but the edge is skipped, the result is 1.25. In this example the linear contribution adds another 0.20 to the coefficient of the whole window. The check is not reduced to a remark about a less warm frame: the forgotten edge node also gives a definite loss.

At a temperature difference of 20 K, the model gives 2.9 × 20 = 58 W of heat transfer. Erroneous application of Ug to the whole unit would give 2 × 1 × 20 = 40 W. The difference of 18 W relates to one considered window and the given temperature difference. Annual heating consumption requires climate, regime and the other components of the balance.

Why the catalog number cannot be distributed to all historic windows

The window openings of a monument may have different glazing bar layouts. With a different proportion of muntins, the frame area changes, and with glazing divided into several parts, the relevant edge length changes. Even the same glazing unit does not make all units identical in Uw. For a bill of quantities it is useful to group truly identical executions and keep the link between the calculation and their dimensions.

At the same time, the thermal calculation does not provide a basis for independently changing the historic pattern for a smaller frame share. Conditions for preserving window infill and technical requirements are considered jointly in the design solution. Substitution of characteristics creates only the appearance of such task coordination: on paper the window becomes suitable, whereas the specified thermal condition remained unfulfilled.

A separate subject is the junction of the unit to the wall. In our comparison we consider the characteristic of the window unit itself, without the mounting node. For an installed window, the source additionally highlights the corresponding linear contribution of the junction. It is assessed within its own boundary; there is no basis to consider the installation ideal just because Uw has been found.

The linear coefficient has a different dimension than Ug and Uf. Therefore it is first multiplied by the edge length, not by the glazing area. Each term of the numerator is then expressed in W/K. Such a unit check helps detect another common calculation error: adding the ψg value directly to the coefficient of the whole unit.

What to fix in product selection

The glazing unit can keep its confirmed Ug = 1.0: the error arose when this value was extended to another object. The selection table should show Uw = 1.45 and a negative result relative to the design 1.2. Then a suitable execution with related characteristics is considered, rather than replacing the designation next to the old number.

If the offer for heritage windows is confirmed only by a glazing unit passport, submit the dimensions and the task of design review to NPI "Nedra". Analysis of the unit composition makes it possible to establish the specific missing result before procurement and link thermal properties with the intended historic execution.
